title: Стоп-лист и признание гостьи  (The Stop-List and the Guest's Confession)

segments.t: Escalating the feud with Vika, Chef Barinov forbids the waitresses from stepping past the kitchen line and places half the menu on the stop-list. Out in the dining room, Max apologizes to his older guest, who confesses that she actually comes to Claude Monet for a certain young man.
Вы знаете, Максим, я хочу вам признаться.
Вам, видимо, нравится, как я готовлю?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.

'Ah, so that is how you want to play it, huh?' Wondering if that is how Sasha wants to play it huh shows Max caught off guard. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'Now listen to my new order.' With the moment and menu in play, Sasha keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'Entering is strictly forbidden.' Claiming that entering is strictly forbidden sounds confident, even if Sasha has doubts.

'And just what are you going to do about it?' Sasha asks whether just what are Max going to do about it, refusing to let the point slide. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.

'What are you doing? Quiet down!' Wondering what Sasha doing is cuts straight through the tension between Max and Sasha. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'I was not the one who started this war.' Realizing that she was not the one who started this war changes how Sasha handles the situation.

'Have you lost your minds completely?' Asking whether Sasha lost Sasha's minds completely cuts straight through the tension between Max and Sasha. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'Those items are on the stop-list.' Even though those items are on the stop list, Sasha keeps a steady face in front of Max.
'That is quite alright, Maxim.' Admitting that that is quite alright Maxim shows Max being honest for a change.
Вы знаете, Максим, я хочу вам признаться.

'You know, Maxim, I want to make a confession to you.' Saying that Maxim she wants to make a confession to Max is how Sasha sets the tone with Max. Notice how she sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
'Yes, I noticed that.' With the conversation and menu in play, Max keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
Вам, видимо, нравится, как я готовлю?
'You apparently really like the way I cook?' Questioning whether Max apparently really like the way she cooks is how Sasha tests Max's story.

'I come here for the sake of one young man.' Coming here for the sake of one young man moves the conversation forward without extra drama. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Вы знаете, Максим, я хочу вам признаться.
Вам, видимо, нравится, как я готовлю?

That wraps up this scene as chef Barinov retaliates against Vika by banning waitresses from the kitchen and putting dishes on the stop-list, while the older guest hints to Max that she comes there just to see him. See you next time!
